summary:
CubeSat Mission Designer

CubeSat Mission Designer is an interactive educational game that introduces players to the basics of designing a small satellite mission (CubeSat).

Players act as satellite mission designers and progress through three levels of increasing difficulty. They choose scientific objectives, such as monitoring vegetation, measuring surface temperature, and observing clouds. For each objective, they select suitable wavelengths, scientific instruments, and system configurations.

The game checks players' choices and provides instant feedback. Correct answers earn coins, while incorrect answers cost hearts. Players can use their coins to unlock and customize rocket designs before launching their missions.

The game features a space-themed interface, visual changes based on wavelength selections, sound effects, and animated launch sequences. It also saves players' coins and unlocked designs using local storage on the same browser.

We developed the project using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. HTML builds the game structure, CSS controls its design and animations, and JavaScript manages gameplay, scientific choices, scoring, and interactions.

Our goal is to make space science more accessible and enjoyable through interactive learning and gamification. Future improvements could include orbital simulations, real satellite data, and 3D or virtual reality experiences.
details:
CubeSat Mission Designer is an interactive educational game that helps players understand how small satellite missions are designed. Players act as mission designers and complete three levels of increasing difficulty. They select scientific objectives, such as monitoring vegetation, measuring surface temperature, and observing clouds. Then, they choose suitable wavelengths, scientific instruments, and system configurations for each objective.

The game checks their choices and provides instant feedback. Correct answers earn coins, while incorrect answers cost hearts. Players can use coins to unlock and customize rockets before launching their missions through an animated sequence.

Our project aims to make space science easier and more engaging, especially for students, by combining scientific concepts with gamification. It encourages logical thinking, decision-making, and learning through experimentation.

We developed the game using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. HTML creates the structure, CSS controls the visual design and animations, and JavaScript manages the game logic, interactions, scoring system, and saved progress using local storage. We also used browser-based tools to develop and test the game.

The creative aspect is the combination of satellite mission design with a progressive game experience, allowing players to explore scientific decisions in an interactive way. Our team considered scientific relevance, ease of use, increasing difficulty, visual design, and accessibility when developing the project. Future development could include real satellite datasets and more advanced mission simulations.
